Year of 193 CE in the Roman Empire, in which five men claimed the throne and the guard sold it.

After commodus was murdered on the last day of 192, the senate chose an old general, Pertinax. He tried to cut spending and stop the Praetorian Guard from running wild. They killed him in the palace in March, after only 87 days.

The guard then put the throne up for auction. Didius Julianus, a rich senator, won by offering each man a huge payment. Few in Rome or the provinces accepted him. Armies on the frontiers named their own commanders: Septimius Severus on the Danube, Pescennius Niger in Syria, and Clodius Albinus in Britain.

Severus marched on Rome first. Julianus was put to death by the senate in June. Severus defeated Niger in 194 and Albinus in 197, and made himself sole ruler, founding the Severan dynasty. He then dismissed the old guard. See septimius-severus.
sum: Year of 193 CE in the Roman Empire, in which five men claimed the throne and the guard sold it.
